chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about a tailor (or fuller) to whom I had entrusted a garment, and he claimed it was stolen from among his belongings. He said: 'He must establish proof that it was stolen from among his belongings, and there is no liability on him. And if all his belongings were stolen, there is no liability on him.'

key_terms.قَصَّارٍ: Tailor or fuller (one who cleans/presses clothes)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is no liability on him

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a trustee to be exempt from paying for a lost entrusted item due to theft?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the standard of proof for a trustee (*mu'ir*) claiming exemption from liability due to theft, requiring them to substantiate that the loss occurred within their custody. Notably, it establishes that total loss of the trustee's own goods does not automatically negate their claim, provided the specific theft of the entrusted item is proven. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that the burden of proof lies with the party seeking exemption from financial responsibility.
